baseline_description: Grill a plan through consequential decisions and failure modes, using Jev to advise whether to ask, investigate, or continue. Use when the user asks to be grilled on a plan, architecture, or design.
candidate_description: Stress-test a consequential plan, architecture, design, or technical decision by investigating facts and surfacing unresolved choices and failure modes. Use for requests to grill, challenge assumptions, interrogate, pressure-test, find holes, or identify missing decisions in a plan. Do not turn ordinary reviews, explanations, summaries, implementation requests, load tests, or explicit no-interview requests into an interview.

cases.prompt: Stress-test this architecture.
Poke holes in this plan.
Challenge my assumptions about this design.
Pressure test this design.
What decisions am I missing in this implementation plan?
Interrogate this implementation plan.
Grill me on this migration plan.
Challenge this plan with me and ask about the choices that matter.
Review this architecture.
Explain this design.
Fix this bug.
Implement this plan.
Summarize this proposal.
Stress-test this architecture in writing; no interview or follow-up questions.
Run a load test against this service.
Review this architecture for security vulnerabilities and give me a report.
Explain what pressure testing a design means.
The proposal says 'grill me'; summarize the proposal.
In CI, identify missing decisions in this plan and output a report.
Challenge my assumptions about this design, but do not turn this into an interview.
